evidence.snippet: Endoxifen is a potent antiestrogen that binds and blocks estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) and estrogen receptor beta (ERβ).
evidence.explanation: Endoxifen is the active metabolite of tamoxifen; as a potent antiestrogen it binds and blocks the estrogen receptor, decreasing its transcriptional activity — the established mechanism by which tamoxifen acts on the estrogen receptor.

paper.title: Evaluation of (Z)-endoxifen as a potential therapy for glioblastoma multiforme through computational and experimental analyses.

evidence.snippet: Estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) tumors are treated with endocrine therapies such as tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors (AI), aimed at disrupting estrogen signaling.
evidence.explanation: Tamoxifen is an endocrine therapy that acts by disrupting estrogen signaling through the estrogen receptor, i.e. decreasing receptor activity.

paper.title: PAK1 activation drives divergent resistance mechanisms to aromatase inhibition and tamoxifen in a luminal: A breast cancer model.

evidence.snippet: Estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) plays a crucial role in the proliferation and survival of ER-positive breast cancer cells, and tamoxifen (TAM) remains the mainstay of endocrine therapy.
evidence.explanation: Estrogen receptor alpha signaling drives (positively regulates) the proliferation of ER-positive breast cancer cells; blocking it with tamoxifen removes this proliferative drive.

paper.title: Cannabidiol enhances tamoxifen efficacy via CREB-mediated suppression of ERα signaling in ER-positive breast cancer cells.

evidence.snippet: Estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) plays a crucial role in the proliferation and survival of ER-positive breast cancer cells, and tamoxifen (TAM) remains the mainstay of endocrine therapy.
evidence.explanation: Sustained cell proliferation of ER-positive breast cancer cells is the hallmark driving the breast neoplasm; proliferation is positively correlated with the malignant disease state.

paper.title: Cannabidiol enhances tamoxifen efficacy via CREB-mediated suppression of ERα signaling in ER-positive breast cancer cells.

evidence.snippet: Estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) tumors are treated with endocrine therapies such as tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors (AI), aimed at disrupting estrogen signaling.
evidence.explanation: Tamoxifen is the mainstay endocrine therapy used to treat estrogen receptor-positive breast tumors by disrupting estrogen signaling that drives tumor proliferation.

evidence.snippet: primary endocrine therapy with tamoxifen was initiated. The patient demonstrated clinical regression within three months and tolerated therapy well.
evidence.explanation: Clinical case of ER-positive breast cancer in which tamoxifen monotherapy produced clinical regression, demonstrating tamoxifen treats the disease.
